definition: A statistical technique that transforms data into a new set of orthogonal variables (principal components) ranked by how much variance they explain.
details: PCA is a classic dimensionality-reduction method used for data visualization, noise reduction, and as a preprocessing step before other machine learning algorithms.

explainer.lead: PCA transforms data into a new set of orthogonal variables, the principal components, ranked by how much variance each explains. It matters as a classic dimensionality-reduction method for visualization, noise reduction, and preprocessing.

tiers.eli5: You describe a crowd by a few overall directions, like height and width, instead of listing every single measurement, keeping the directions that vary most.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use PCA to shrink feature sets and denoise before other machine learning algorithms. A pitfall is that components are linear and ranked by variance, so directions with small variance but real signal can be dropped.
tiers.paperLevel: Principal component analysis is a statistical technique that transforms data into a new set of orthogonal variables (principal components) ranked by how much variance they explain.

explainer.example: Reducing a hundred-correlated-sensor dataset to two principal components lets you plot the samples while retaining most of the variance.
